title: Run Lola Run
events_chronological: Manni phones Lola in a panic: he has left 100,000 marks in a bag on the U-Bahn and has twenty minutes to hand it to Ronnie.
Lola runs out of the flat past her mother on the telephone and down the stairwell past a woman with a pram and a growling dog.
Lola reaches her father's bank and finds him with his mistress Jutta, who has just told him she is pregnant.
Her father refuses her the money, tells her he is not her father, and has her thrown out.
Lola arrives too late; Manni has robbed a supermarket, and in the getaway a policeman shoots Lola dead.
In the second run Lola is tripped on the stairs and reaches the bank a moment later.
Her father, mid-argument with Jutta, slaps her, and Lola takes the security guard's gun and robs the bank herself.
Lola gets out with the money and finds Manni, who is run over by an ambulance in front of her.
In the third run Lola is a moment earlier on the stairs and misses her father entirely, seeing him drive away with his colleague Meyer.
Lola walks into a casino, buys a single chip, and screams the roulette ball into 20 twice to win 129,000 marks.
In this run Manni spots the tramp who took his bag and chases him down on foot.
Manni gets the money back at gunpoint and hands it to Ronnie with seconds to spare.
Lola arrives carrying a bag of her own, and Manni asks what is in it.
Between the runs, Lola and Manni lie in bed in red light asking each other whether the other really loves them.
Each run rewrites the futures of the strangers Lola passes - the woman with the pram, the office worker Doris, the cyclist - shown in bursts of snapshots.
Her father's fate diverges with every run: publicly exposed, robbed by his own daughter, or killed in a crash with Meyer.
syuzhet_notes: The film runs the same twenty minutes three times over, restarting from the telephone call after each ending, so told-order bullets 8 and 11 are hard resets that put the story back where it stood at bullet 2. The two deaths at told-order bullets 6 and 10 are both undone by the next restart, and bullet 7 is a bedroom scene that belongs to none of the three runs.
fabula_notes: The three runs are alternatives rather than a sequence, so this ordering lays them out as successive attempts instead of one causal chain; nothing carries between them except Lola's apparent memory of having done it before. The snapshot futures of the passers-by are flash-forwards decades ahead, and they differ in every run.
